title: Care Assistant - Bank - Care Home
description:
This is a Bank role so no confirmed hours

Shifts -8am to 8pm or 8pm to 8am

We are not accepting sponsorships or switch

ABOUT THE ROLE
This is a casual, part-time role offering flexible working. As a Bank Care Assistant at a Barchester care home, you'll help residents enjoy each day by making sure they get the quality care and support they deserve. You'll assist with daily living, providing support and companionship and sharing great moments and memories too. It's a chance to bring your dedication and compassion to a fulfilling environment. Every day will be different, so you can expect to undertake work that's as varied as it is rewarding. As a Bank Care Assistant, you could be doing anything from supporting residents with their food and drink and following care plans to ensuring that each of our residents has one-to-one time. It's an opportunity to put your skills to meaningful use and develop your career.

ABOUT YOU
To join us as a Bank Care Assistant you'll need to have some experience of caring for older people, a can-do approach and excellent communication skills. Your empathy and warm-hearted approach will shine through, but above all, you'll have the compassion needed to deliver the highest standard of care and support for all our residents. In return we'll provide all the training you need to thrive.

REWARDS PACKAGE
As well as competitive pay, you can look forward to a role that offers true flexibility and plenty of free learning and development opportunities. As one of the UK's leading healthcare providers, we take the growth of everyone who works for us seriously.

As this is a Bank position to provide cover as and when we need it, such as for annual leave or sick leave, the hours and days you work will vary.

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality care you'd expect for your loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

title: Support Worker - Clouds House
description:
Support Worker Clouds House

Location: Clouds House

Salary: £28,479 per annum

About The Role

Looking for work where you can truly make a difference?

Join the team at Clouds House as a Support Worker, based at Clouds House. You ll play a vital role in helping people build lasting recovery in a safe, structured and therapeutic residential environment.

Working within our fully integrated One Team model, you ll help reinforce our 12-Step and trauma-informed treatment approach. No two shifts are the same this is a hands-on, rewarding role where your presence, professionalism and compassion matter every day.

What you ll be doing:
- Supporting clients to engage in daily routines, wellbeing activities and the therapeutic programme
- Promoting structure, communal responsibilities and positive recovery habits
- Maintaining a safe, respectful and supportive living environment
- Monitoring welfare, safeguarding and behavioural concerns, escalating where needed
- Supporting medication processes (including eMAR where trained)
- Completing accurate, up-to-date records and handovers
- Responding calmly and professionally to incidents or client needs
- Working closely with colleagues across all departments as part of one team

What we re looking for:
- Experience in health, social care, recovery or residential settings
- Strong communication and people skills
- Emotional resilience with the ability to remain calm under pressure
- A professional, boundaried and compassionate approach
- Good organisation and attention to detail
- Understanding of safeguarding principles
- Commitment to recovery-focused and trauma-informed practice

Desirable:
- Experience in addiction or mental health services
- Knowledge of 12-Step recovery models
- Experience managing challenging behaviour
- Full UK Driving Licence

At Clouds House, you ll be part of a supportive and passionate team making a genuine difference every day. We offer ongoing training and development opportunities, and the chance to build valuable experience in a rewarding recovery-focused environment where your contribution truly matters.

If you re passionate about supporting others and want flexible work in a rewarding setting, we d love to hear from you.

Please note: No sponsorships are available for this role.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. Our services have supported thousands of people to make positive changes and build productive lives with a job, family, friends and a sense of community.

We are committed to our cause and the work we carry out as a charity. Equally the wellbeing and the employees who work for us are also important. Joining us an employee, we will offer you the following benefits -
- Flexible working
- Support for Families We support our employees through every stage of family life by offering enhanced maternity and paternity pay for eligible employees who have completed 26 weeks' continuous service, alongside family-friendly policies and a supportive, inclusive workplace. If you'd like more information about our family-friendly benefits, please contact our Recruitment Team at (url removed)
- Training and development opportunities
- Simply Health Cashback Scheme (optional)
- Season Ticket Loan Scheme
- Cycle to work scheme
- Crisis Loan Scheme
- Electric Car Scheme
- 3 x Wellbeing Days (pro rata'd for part time employees)
- Access to Blue Light Card
- 25 days (rising to 30 with length of service) Annual Leave plus Bank Holidays
- Contributory Pension Scheme Employer matched contributions of up to 6% in the first two years service and up to 9% thereafter
- Death in Service Payment (2x annual salary)
- Critical Illness Insurance (subject to qualifying criteria)

Please note that we may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of suitable applications.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Forward Trust, please click apply to be redirected to our website to complete your application.

title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Role Overview

Affinity Staff is recruiting compassionate and reliable Healthcare Assistants (HCAs) to join our agency team, supporting an established care facility in Calne, Wiltshire.

As a temporary HCA working through Affinity Staff, you will play a vital role in providing high-quality personal care, dignity, and companionship to residents. You will enjoy complete control over your schedule while benefiting from our dedicated, round-the-clock support.

Key Responsibilities
- Assisting residents with daily personal care, dressing, hygiene, and mobility needs.
- Supporting meal times, nutrition monitoring, and encouraging hydration.
- Promoting dignity, independence, and person-centred care at all times.
- Maintaining accurate care records and daily fluid/food intake documentation.
- Collaborating with senior carers and nursing staff to ensure a safe, supportive environment.

Requirements
- Minimum 6 months of experience in a UK healthcare or care home setting.
- NVQ Level 2 in Health & Social Care (preferred but not essential).
- Enhanced DBS check registered on the Update Service (or willing to process a new one).
- Valid Right to Work in the UK.
- Caring, reliable nature with excellent communication skills.

Benefits of Working with Affinity Staff
- Competitive Market Rates with prompt weekly pay.
- 24/7 Support: Dedicated consultants available round-the-clock to assist you.
- Total Flexibility: Choose the shifts that fit around your lifestyle and commitments.
- Fast-track registration process and easy shift booking.

How to Apply

Click Apply Now on CV-Library to join Affinity Staff or contact the Affinity Staff recruitment team to get registered immediately.
